source.description: An incident of this source is a Case: same identifier, its alerts the Case's alerts, its evidence the Case's observables.

unknown.name: Informational
unknown.note: the source says nothing; the Case starts at the bottom and triage sets it

resolved.name: Resolved
resolved.note: the source's own closure; the engine's is Closed, and the two are not the same event

redirected.name: Closed
redirected.note: merged into another incident: the Case closes as a Duplicate of its master

unknown.name: Unknown
unknown.note: the source has not classified the incident, which is how every incident starts and how many are left when they are resolved there

informationalExpectedActivity.name: Benign
informationalExpectedActivity.note: activity that was real and expected: the framework's Benign, authorized activity that legitimately matched the detection

rules.alert_type: Inbox forwarding / redirect or hide rule
Unsanctioned SaaS app usage (Shadow IT / Shadow AI discovery)
Mass sensitive-file access by one principal

case_map.ignored: the source's title for the incident; the Case's account is its Notes, and a title nobody wrote is not one
when the source opened its record. The Case's start_time is when the adversary acted, which is the earliest alert activity, and its own lifecycle is in its events
the analyst thread on the source's record. The engine reads it to see whether its own write-back is already there, and a comment is not Case data: the Case's account is its Notes
one entry of the analyst thread: its text. A writer of Notes to the source reads the thread so as not to write the same Note twice; nothing of it lands on the Case
who wrote the entry, as a display name — a person's or an application's. It is not an identity the Case can cite
when the entry was written. With the entry it belongs to: on the source's thread, not on the Case
the source's own narrative of the incident, generated from its alerts. What §1.1 requires is each alert's description, which is read; the Case's account is its Notes
the source's generated summary. Empty on every record observed at this licence tier, and listed so that the day the source fills it is a day somebody decides where it lands
the source's own 0–100 priority for its queue. The Case's severity is assessed by triage (§1.4), and a second, unexplained score beside it would be weighed by nobody
who last changed the source's record, as a display name — a person's or an application's. Not an identity the Case can cite, and not a time a poller can resume from
the remark left on the source's record when it was resolved there. The Case's closure is stated by its Note, which is what is written back
the operator's own tags on the source's record. Nothing in the framework reads them, and a deployment that wants them says so here rather than having them appear on a Case unexamined
the source's own tags on the incident. Same: read by nothing, and recorded here so that a tag the vendor starts sending is not silence
the API's own envelope, not the record

case_map.note: It lands twice. As the severity of the Detection Finding that represents the alert, the event the Alert Finding cites. And as that Finding's confidence (the zerosoc:confidence_id tag: Informational and Low give Low, Medium gives Medium, High and Critical give High) — a workaround, because this source states no confidence of its own for an alert. How bad and how sure are two measures, and the day the source states the second this entry stops borrowing the first.

the source's own procedure. It reaches the Case as the disposition of each recommendation — the Finding a followed one produced, or the Finding that states why it was set aside — never as a block of text on the alert

case_map.ignored: which Defender workload raised the alert. detectionSource is the finer of the two and is what the analytic carries; this one is kept out rather than recorded twice
the workload's own id for the alert, before Defender gave it one. The Case cites the alert by the id Defender publishes, which is what a reader can open
the alert's back-reference to the incident: the Case is that incident, so the link is the Case's own uid
the tenant, already on the Case once from the incident; an alert of another tenant is refused at intake
the source's own kill-chain category. The framework's alert type comes from the alert_types rules of this profile and its Incident Category from the playbook, neither of which reads this
the source's per-alert triage state. The Case has one status, and it is the executor's
the source's per-alert verdict. The Case's verdict is the engine's own, and the source's sits on the incident's extension where it is visible without being weighed
as classification: the source's per-alert determination
the source's per-alert assignment. The Case has one assignee, and it is set by the method, not inherited from an alert
the source's kill-chain categories for the alert, as a list; category is the older single value. The framework's alert type comes from the alert_types rules, never from these
the source's own tags on the alert. As the incident's: read by nothing, and listed so that a tag that starts to carry meaning is noticed
the analyst thread of one alert. Notes are written to the incident's thread, and this one is read by nothing

the state of the source's own automated investigation of the alert. It says whether the product investigated, which bears on who wrote classification and determination; those are recorded and weighed by nobody, and so is this

the threat actor the source attributes the alert to. Empty on every record observed at this licence tier, and listed so that the day the source fills it is a day somebody decides where it lands: an attribution is a lead for the Malicious hypothesis, as the threat family is

the custom-detection policy behind the alert. detectorId identifies the detector for every alert, custom or not. Empty on every record observed at this licence tier, and listed so that the day the source fills it is a day somebody decides where it lands
the portal's page for the alert. The Case cites the alert by its uid, and the link a reader follows is the incident's, on the extension object
the alert's copy of the incident's link: already on the Case once, from the incident
when the source last changed the alert. A poller resumes from the incident's own time, and the activity times are what the Case's timeline reads
when the alert was resolved on the source. The Case's own closure is the one that counts
a free-form bag the detector may fill. Empty on every alert observed; a key inside it arrives as a path of its own and is caught like any other
the custom detection's own key-value pairs. Empty on every alert observed; a key inside it arrives as a path of its own
the entity's kind, as the API types it. It selects which of the fields below are read and becomes the observable's type_id rather than a value of its own
the source's per-entity verdict. Read by the evidence inventory to show what the source thought; it is not a Finding of the Case, which weighs the evidence itself

what the sensor did at the moment of detection: detected, blocked, prevented. It travels with the evidence row the inventory builds, and reaches the Case only inside a Finding that cites it; the state the method reads for §1.5 is remediationStatus
when the source attached this evidence item to the alert — not when the entity acted. The activity times of the alert are what the timeline reads
the part the source gives the entity in the alert. Empty on every item observed; detailedRoles is where the source writes it
the part the source gives the entity in the alert, in its own words. Which entity a Finding is about is decided by the method from the evidence, not taken from a label
the operator's own tags on the entity. Nothing in the framework reads them; a deployment that gives one a meaning records it in the SOC Knowledge Base
the device's platform. Asset context the enrichment asks the source for at triage, where it is a Finding with its analytic, rather than an unattributed field on the Case
the device's short name, already in deviceDnsName, which the observable carries
the device's DNS domain, already in deviceDnsName
the device's NT domain. Empty on every record observed at this licence tier, and listed so that the day the source fills it is a day somebody decides where it lands

the directory's id for the device. The device is identified by mdeDeviceId and its DNS name. Empty on every record observed at this licence tier, and listed so that the day the source fills it is a day somebody decides where it lands
the device's OS build. Asset context: the enrichment asks the source for the device at triage, and what bears on the Case is stated there as a Finding, with its source
the device's OS version. Asset context: the enrichment asks the source for the device at triage, and what bears on the Case is stated there as a Finding, with its source
the sensor's health on the device. Asset context: the enrichment asks the source for the device at triage, and what bears on the Case is stated there as a Finding, with its source
whether the device is onboarded to the sensor. Asset context: the enrichment asks the source for the device at triage, and what bears on the Case is stated there as a Finding, with its source
the state of the anti-malware engine on the device. Asset context: the enrichment asks the source for the device at triage, and what bears on the Case is stated there as a Finding, with its source
the source's own risk level for the device. How much the asset matters comes from the SOC Knowledge Base; the source's score is read at enrichment and stated as a Finding where it bears
the source's device group, by id. An access-control detail of the source, read by nothing
the source's device group, by name. Empty on every record observed at this licence tier, and listed so that the day the source fills it is a day somebody decides where it lands
when the sensor first saw the device. Asset context: the enrichment asks the source for the device at triage, and what bears on the Case is stated there as a Finding, with its source

the device's last internal address. Asset context: the enrichment asks the source for the device at triage, and what bears on the Case is stated there as a Finding, with its source; an address an alert cites arrives as evidence of its own
the device's last external address. As lastIpAddress: asset context, and never an observable the Case did not get from an alert
every address of the device's interfaces. As lastIpAddress: asset context, and never an observable the Case did not get from an alert
who was logged on to the device when the alert fired. A lead for the identity pivot of the investigation, asked of the source then and stated as a Finding; not an observable by itself
the name of an account logged on to the device, as loggedOnUsers: a lead for the identity pivot, not an observable
the domain of an account logged on to the device, as loggedOnUsers
the resources the device reached. Empty on every item observed

the cloud virtual machine behind the device, where it is one. Asset context: the enrichment asks the source for the device at triage, and what bears on the Case is stated there as a Finding, with its source
as vmMetadata: the cloud it runs in
as vmMetadata: the cloud's resource path
as vmMetadata: the subscription that holds it
as vmMetadata: the virtual machine's own id
where the source geolocated the address. Geolocation is enrichment and reaches the Case as a Finding with what produced it

where the source places the address. Empty on every record observed at this licence tier, and listed so that the day the source fills it is a day somebody decides where it lands; geolocation is enrichment, as countryLetterCode
the network stream the address or the account was seen in. Empty on every record observed at this licence tier, and listed so that the day the source fills it is a day somebody decides where it lands
the account's domain, already in the principal name the observable carries

the account's security identifier. It travels with the evidence row the inventory builds, and reaches the Case only inside a Finding that cites it: it tells a well-known system account from a person's, which the lineage of a process needs

the account's display name. Empty on every record observed at this licence tier, and listed so that the day the source fills it is a day somebody decides where it lands; the observable is the principal name
the on-premises directory's id for the account. Empty on every record observed at this licence tier, and listed so that the day the source fills it is a day somebody decides where it lands

the account's tenant. Empty on every record observed at this licence tier, and listed so that the day the source fills it is a day somebody decides where it lands; the Case carries the tenant once, from the incident
the resources the account reached. Empty on every item observed
where the file was. It travels with the evidence row the inventory builds and with the evidence a Finding rests on; the observable is the hash, which is what a lookup takes
the signature's subject. The signed-publisher check reads it from the evidence row and states it as a Finding, with the check that produced it
as signer: read by the signed-publisher check, not carried unattributed

a second digest of the same file. It travels with the evidence row the inventory builds, and reaches the Case only inside a Finding that cites it, where it helps tell one file from another; the observable is the SHA-256, which every lookup of the method takes
a third digest of the same file, often absent. The observable is the SHA-256
the digest of the file's signature. Empty on every record observed at this licence tier, and listed so that the day the source fills it is a day somebody decides where it lands
the file's size in bytes. Read by nothing
the publisher the source read from the file. As signer: a check of who signed a file states it as a Finding, and it is not carried unattributed
the command line. Evidence a Finding rests on, kept where that Finding cites it, and never an observable: an observable is an entity that can be looked up
the process id, meaningful only with the device and the creation time. The evidence row carries the three together
with processId and the device, the identity of one process instance; on the evidence row, not on the Case as a field
the image's path: with the evidence row, as fileDetails.filePath
as fileDetails.sha1: a second digest of the image, with the evidence row
a third digest of the process image, often absent, as fileDetails.md5. The observable is the SHA-256
the digest of the image's signature, as fileDetails.sha256Ac. Empty on every record observed at this licence tier
the process image's size in bytes, as fileDetails.fileSize. Read by nothing
the publisher the source read from the process image, as fileDetails.filePublisher: stated as a Finding by a check of who signed it, never carried unattributed
the subject of the image's signature, as fileDetails.signer: read from the evidence row by a check of who signed the file
the issuer of the image's signature, as fileDetails.issuer: read with the signer, not carried unattributed
the parent, which the attack graph reads from the evidence rows; on the Case it is an edge, not a field
with parentProcessId, the parent instance; on the evidence row
the parent's image, read with the parent instance on the evidence row

as parentProcessImageFile: read with the parent instance on the evidence row
as parentProcessImageFile: read with the parent instance on the evidence row
as parentProcessImageFile: read with the parent instance on the evidence row
as parentProcessImageFile: read with the parent instance on the evidence row

the hive of a registry key or value the alert cites. It travels with the evidence row the inventory builds, and reaches the Case only inside a Finding that cites it: with registryKey it is the identity of one registry entity on one device
the key's path under its hive. With registryHive, the identity of the registry entity on the evidence row
the name of the value under the key. With the key, on the evidence row

extension.description: What this source states about the incident and the framework has no field for. Nothing the framework carries is repeated here: that would be a mapping, not an extension.

incident_id.description: The source's identifier, which is also the Case's uid; kept so the extension reads whole on its own.

incident_web_url.description: Where an analyst opens the incident in the source's portal.

tenant_id.description: The tenant the incident belongs to; an incident of another tenant is refused at intake.

status.description: The source's own status, in its own word.

classification.description: The source's own verdict, recorded and never weighed: the Case's verdict is the executor's.

determination.description: The source's own determination, on the same terms.

assigned_to.description: Who owns the incident in the source; the Case's assignee is the executor's own.

redirect_incident_id.description: The master this incident was merged into.

last_update_time.description: When the source last changed the record; the poller resumes from it.

asset.cmdb.answers: What is this device: its platform, its risk and exposure, its tags and the value the operator gave it.
limits: a device the endpoint sensor never onboarded is not here

identity.directory.answers: What this source knows about an account: the alerts it appears in and the devices it has used.
limits: this source has no directory record of its own: the account's attributes come from the directory itself, not from here
an account outside the directory — a local account, a guest that never signed in — appears only where an alert named it

malware.repository.answers: What the vendor knows about a file: its own verdict, its signer, and how widely it has been seen.
limits: a hash the vendor has never seen returns no record, which is an answer and not a gap
prevalence is this tenant's and the vendor's, not the world's

reputation.multi_engine.answers: What this source has seen of an address or a domain: the alerts it appears in and its prevalence here.
limits: this is one vendor's sight of the indicator, not a multi-engine consensus: the class is named for what the method wants, and this source answers the narrower question
an address the tenant has never contacted has no statistics, which is not a verdict

cases.store.answers: Has this entity been in an incident before, and how were those incidents determined.
limits: the source's own incident history only, bounded by its retention

telemetry.endpoint.answers: What ran, what was written, what connected, on a device.
limits: advanced hunting is not available on every licence tier
the hunting tables are retained for 30 days

telemetry.identity.answers: Sign-ins and directory changes for an account.
limits: identity tables are empty where the identity workload is not deployed

process_events.asks: What ran on this device, in this window?
process_events.recipe: DeviceProcessEvents | where DeviceId =~ '{device}' or DeviceName =~ '{device}' | limit {limit}
limits: 30-day retention
advanced hunting is not on every licence tier

file_events.asks: What was written, renamed or deleted on this device?
file_events.recipe: DeviceFileEvents | where DeviceId =~ '{device}' or SHA256 =~ '{hash}' | limit {limit}
limits: 30-day retention

network_events.asks: What did this device connect to?
network_events.recipe: DeviceNetworkEvents | where RemoteIP =~ '{ip}' or LocalIP =~ '{ip}' | limit {limit}
limits: 30-day retention

logon_events.asks: Who logged on to this device, and how?
logon_events.recipe: DeviceLogonEvents | where DeviceId =~ '{device}' or AccountUpn =~ '{user}' | limit {limit}
limits: 30-day retention

registry_events.asks: What was written to the registry on this device?
limits: 30-day retention

sign_ins.asks: Where did this account sign in from?
limits: the table is in preview and absent on lower tiers
sign-in retention is shorter than the endpoint tables on some licences

email_messages.asks: What did this message do, and who else received it?
email_messages.recipe: EmailEvents | where SenderFromAddress =~ '{sender}' or NetworkMessageId =~ '{id}' | limit {limit}
limits: needs the collaboration workload

related_cases.asks: Has this entity been in an incident before?
limits: the source's own incidents only

directory_changes.asks: What changed on this account or group, and who changed it?
directory_changes.recipe: IdentityDirectoryEvents | where AccountUpn =~ '{user}' or TargetAccountUpn =~ '{user}' | limit {limit}
limits: needs the identity workload deployed against the domain controllers
